action: Starts from a plain sphere and makes straight slice cuts across it, the first one taking off the side to make a flat cheek/side plane.
why: Turn the round ball into a head with flat anime side planes from the first minute.
reader_equivalent: UV sphere -> Edit Mode bisect (Fill off) or Sculpt Line Project / Trim Line

action: Adds more slice cuts so the sphere becomes a faceted block: flat front face plane, flat side plane, a cut-off jaw/underside and a chamfered top, with the cut lines staying as hard edges.
why: Lock in the face plane, jaw angle and skull box as flat planes before any detail.
reader_equivalent: Repeated bisect planes or Sculpt Line Project with the view rotated per plane

action: Pulls the lower face/chin forward and down with a large brush on the faceted block, keeping the flat planes above.
tool: Move (large draw size, inferred from the big red ring and bulge)
why: Set jaw and chin length and projection from the side.

action: From a view below the chin, pulls a pointed nose out of the face plane as a small sharp wedge and starts shaping the cheek-to-nose plane.
tool: Move / Snake Hook (inferred from the pulled spike)
why: Anime nose is a small sharp point; checking from below confirms its projection and the face plane width.
reader_equivalent: Snake Hook or Grab, then Pinch on the bridge

action: Rough face now has a narrow straight nose, a closed mouth line with a defined upper lip, brow ridge and soft eye sockets; he strokes around the eye area.
why: Build the secondary forms (sockets, lips, nose bridge) on top of the planar block.
reader_equivalent: Clay Strips + Smooth, Draw for the lip line

action: Masks a large oval over each eye socket (shown dark grey) and works inside/around the masked area.
tool: Mask brush (MaskPen) then a sculpt brush
why: Isolate the eye regions so the socket shape can be pushed/defined without disturbing the cheeks and brow.
reader_equivalent: Mask brush (or Box/Lasso Mask), then Draw/Clay with mask protecting the rest

action: From the side view, draws the outer eye contour with a small brush, checking the eye sits back from the nose and brow in profile.
why: The eye depth and outer corner placement are judged in profile.

action: Cuts the eye opening as a large almond-shaped inset with a flat recessed plane inside and a sharp lid edge; the ear is already present and the mouth is a single crease line.
tool: carving/flatten brush inside the eye outline (not readable)
why: Anime eyes are big flat recessed areas bounded by crisp lid lines, not spherical eyeballs.
reader_equivalent: Crease the outline, then Flatten/Scrape (subtract) inside; or mask the almond and Draw subtract

action: Rotates to an extreme under-chin view and smooths/strokes the cheek and jaw plane.
why: Check the jaw and cheek volume from below where anime faces often look wrong.
reader_equivalent: Smooth / Clay Strips while orbiting under the chin

action: Rotates/tilts the head with the Gizmo, then opens the brush palette (visible: Move, ClayBuildup, ClayTubes, Inflat, SnakeHook, hPolish, ZRemesher, ZModeler, TrimCurve, Smooth, Rake, XMD2).
why: Pose the head and pick the next brush; the palette shows his working brush set.
reader_equivalent: Rotate with gizmo (or Pose brush); Grab, Clay Strips, Clay, Inflate, Snake Hook, Flatten/Scrape, Crease, Smooth

action: Shows the finished Gojo bust: spiky hair made of many separate pointed, curved, tapered locks each with a groove down its length, a cloth blindfold band, small almond eyes and long-fingered hand posed in front of the face.
why: Target result: crisp individual locks stacked in layers, hard silhouette.
reader_equivalent: Separate lock meshes (Snake Hook from a sphere or curve tubes) with Crease down the middle and Pinch on the edges
